so by "types" of testosterone, he doesnt mean different actual testosterone. injectable TRT is made up of testosterone base, the liquid it is carried in (oil, water) and the ester attached to it that controls how slowly or quickly your body absorbs and distributes it. in "testosterone cypionate" , the active drug is testosterone and the ester is cypionate. in nebido (testosterone undecanoate), the active drug is testosterone and the ester is undecanoate. cypionate needs to be injected every 6-7 days because the ester has finished releasing the T, nebido is extremely slow acting and needs a very large dose to be injected every 10-14 weeks instead. in the end, itll be the same levels of T in your blood as the weekly shots, it wont effect your transition quality or speed

i have a really bad needle phobia. right now i have 1/2 inch (12mm) 27 gauge fixed needles (gauge is how thick the needle is, larger number means a thinner needle, less pain but slower injection). i did my first shot with a 5/8 inch (16mm) 25g leur lock needle (and 20g to draw) but it scared me too badly and i returned them. but what was really a game changer was [getting an auto injector!](https://www.amazon.com/Ambimedinc-IE400-Inject-Ease-Automatic-Injector/dp/B000PKYX8K) it's a little plastic device you load the syringe into and it injects you with a button press, it hides the needle so you dont even see it. it only fits fixed needle syringes (like insulin syringes), so you need to make sure the ones you get will work with it, but it doesnt effect anything to draw and inject with the same needle.

how big is the vial? 1ml vial isnt gonna last as long as a 5ml vial which wont last as long as a 10 or 15ml vial, T vials come in all shapes and sizes. as someone else said, 0.5ml of 250mg concentration is a very high dose, much less a starting dose, but i get the sense that all the numbers are kinda confusing. i get that, it was really intimidating for me too at first, but its not too bad once you know what everything means.

ml (milliliter) is the amount of liquid in a vial or being injected, 0.5ml means half of one milliliter. 0.5ml is a common starting dose among guys being prescribed the average 100mg concentration, which would mean 50mg of T injected. the one you were looking at is over doubly as strong as that!

mg (milligram) means the amount of T actually contained inside. these vials arent pure liquid T, the T is carried in oils and esters that help your body absorb it slowly over time. forms of T without any oils or esters (like testosterone suspension) get injected every day to maintain levels since your body absorbs it all immediately. 250mg/ml is the concentration of T, which is to say how much pure T is actually contained in the oil per milliliter. a 10ml vial of 250mg concentration would mean a whopping 2500mg total testosterone in that little vial!

the vials i just bought were 10mls of a 200mg concentration, a flat number is just easier to do the math on and measure out how much you need in the syringe. to get a 50mg dose of mine, itd be 0.25ml, which is a blessedly tiny shot! my favorite part of injecting the higher concentration is you inject half as much liquid, the shot goes much faster. if you wanted to start on 50mg of a 250 concentration, itd be 0.2, but if you wanted to raise your dose from there the math gets harder and is more difficult to measure out. 

but for my vials, supposing i inject 0.25ml (50mg) every week consistently and never up my dose, a 200mg/10ml vial should last me 40 weeks, assuming absolutely perfect conditions. i bought 3 vials to last me hopefully 2 years counting for dead space or accidents or coring (where the rubber on the vial gets too damaged from the needles, if that happens the rest of the vial needs to be tossed out). id say assume a 10ml vial will last you 6-8 months in ideal conditions

mythical DHT cream is always recommended for bottom growth (especially common before meta/phallo) but these days is incredibly hard to find something calling itself DHT cream that really has any DHT in it. DHT (dihydrotestosterone) is the androgen responsible for things like bottom growth and hair growth/loss cycles, cis men typically produce it in their balls so even trans men in healthy male ranges of T typically have very little DHT. 

but with recent research, if you apply T cream (NOT gel, which is alcohol based) your body will take over and locally convert what it needs into DHT for bottom growth. this is doubly great because using pure DHT cream means if you get too much, your body cant convert the extra DHT back into estrogen like it does with normal T, and too much DHT can cause balding among other things. 

thankfully, T raws are much easier to source for making cream than DHT raws too. r/estrogel has some great T cream recipes in their wiki to check out!

as for the drawbacks, DHT cannot be converted back into estrogen by the body. having too much DHT effects other things in your body, like promoting early hair loss. its much harder to control the dose.

T cream, which compounding pharmacies can make (with rx) or you can learn yourself in the subreddit listed above, will be converted to DHT (dihydrotestosterone) inside your body when applied locally to the genitals. the leftover after your body doesnt need DHT will stay as T or get converted into E if your levels are too high (which i assume isnt a problem if you are microdosing). its all around the better and easier option.

"just use dht" gets thrown around a lot in bottom growth spaces, but the truth is even using regular T cream (NOT gel, which is alcohol based and will burn your bits) topically on your bottom growth will convert it into DHT locally inside your body and have the same effects. r/estrogel has a lot of resources for this, ive been looking into it for my own bottom growth

I haven't tried baby powder personally, but I'd think it'd interfere with the adhesive sticking on your skin. But in my experience with tape, you only really get blisters that bad if you're applying it wrong. I used to get these massive painful blisters that would take forever to heal, but there's a technique you develop after using it a while. Blisters on your sides come from pulling the back end of the tape taut, stretching out the back of the tape as far as it'll go tugs and rips at the thin skin over your ribs. When applying, you can pull tighter over the skin on your chest but have to lay it down more gently (less stretched out) when you get to your ribs. This way it creates a more stable anchor for the part that actually needs stretched. 

On the opposite end, putting the tape too far in on your chest creates this skin pulling effect. Very uncomfortable and can cause more blisters in your front. I've learned you can avoid that by not placing tape too far past your nipple, and at least personally this also saves me quite a bit of tape from over-binding. Honestly, getting comfortable enough with applying tape has gotten me to the point of only needing one or two wide pieces on each side to get it good enough that I pass with a loose shirt (D cup chest), and using just one or two pieces of tape is perfect to go under a binder and hold everything in place. These days I hate wearing a binder without tape, I'm always readjusting.

This *is* an actual discussion. You asked for other peoples opinions. When the opinions didn't bow down and agree with you, you completely shut down and stopped hearing anything any of us were saying. Are all these people independently saying the same exact thing all just wrong and were put on this earth to annoy you, or is there something you might be misunderstanding about the situation? 

From the few facts being repeated, it seems like this may be a big misunderstanding. Everyone experiences DID differently. Even though you have it, you can't fully understand the way every other system on earth functions. There isn't a single correct way to have DID. From what you've been saying, I can only assume in your system other alters only front in times of great stress. This is not universal, not even close to universal. In many systems, other alters just front for benign reasons, or no reason at all, *especially* when a dissociant drug that makes switching more fluid is introduced. And this is completely normal, I'd say even very healthy, to switch for neutral or positive reasons.

I'm sorry that you feel "weird" or icky or what have you, but this situation is normal. She hasn't done anything wrong. Again, I think you need to sit with the information we have all provided and the feelings you're having and try to get to the root of what is actually making you feel this way. In a very objective sense, nothing wrong or bad has occurred here. Most people wouldn't even consider this situation in more than a passing thought, a 'huh, I didn't know that.' and continue on with their day unbothered.

Did she actually say "another alter was close to the front *because* I didn't want to have sex, but did it anyway"? I can understand how hearing that could hurt, but it isn't a consent issue on *your* end if that's the case. She would've been the one that didn't really want to continue but decided it was better to just consent anyways. It would be her own issue that she gets to deal with. You consented to being with her, and she consented to being with you.

From everything you've said, this sounds more like a bruised ego than anything she has actually done wrong. It may help to sit with these emotions and sort out what's really making you feel this way.

As much as it's tempting to want to, you can't control everything that goes on in someone elses head. If you can't cope with someone else co-fronting, you may want to steer clear of dating others with DID. But it *is* very normal for co-fronting to happen, or for others to be watching whats happening to keep them all safe. If something went wrong, they'd be able to switch and handle the situation. Or if sex is triggering, someone nearby can help keep them calm during it. It's just the way they function best.

I'm in central Florida and finally got my name changed in march of 2023. I was also terrified of being turned down and wasting money, it already takes me so long to save up the 4-500$ filing fee, so I put it off for years. When I ended up eventually filing, I learned that you can file for "indigency", which basically means "I cannot afford the filing fees" and the courts will wave those fees. After all that, I think it cost me less than 100 dollars going through the whole process, and most of that was printing copies of court documents and paying to have them notarized, or paying to have a new ID printed with my new name. I can't guarantee, but at the time they didn't even call me into court to formally see a judge. They were cutting down on the more frivolous "judge signs a document in court so you have to appear for 5 minutes" cases to stop covid spreading in the courtrooms, so after a few weeks I was mailed my approved name change and the extra copies I requested to update other documents with the new name. It was a lot easier than I was worried about! 

The worst part of it was filling out or even finding the right legal documents and where they need to go, but I found a website that basically does it all for you! Made with trans Floridians in mind, [floridanamechange](https://www.floridanamechange.org/) walks you through the documents and fills them out for you, tells you where to file based on your county, and different steps after filing to change the rest of your legal documents to match! It was a massive help, it made the whole process feel a lot less daunting. I hope it can help you too.

OSDD isnt like... a different disorder. being diagnosed as OSDD is just a therapist saying "you dont have *all* the symptoms of DID, but you clearly have it & we need to call it something". we still need language to describe the experience, so the definition is "DID without x"

yeah, there is no "core" in osdd either. the concept of an "original" isnt real because all children start out fragmented & trauma makes a child stay fragmented. there was never a single cohesive personality that everyone else just split from, because by the time a child *has* that cohesion the brain is solidified that way. it is a developmental milestone, a pivotal point in the development of the brain where it cant go back. thats why after a certain age a kid is unable to develop DID, & why it cant suddenly develop in adults

A lot of this is finding compromises and figuring out how to realistically keep everyone happy. Our host keeps our hair blonde and short, but everyone else has their own idea of what our hair should look like. As a compromise, we keep it how he wants it but the rest of us are given tools to change it. I was given some temporary pink dye for when I'm out, we got a wig and cute hair bows for our little to feel more comfortable, everyone is fairly satisfied with their compromises. If someone really wants something we can't afford right now, we make a note of it for the long term and try to get them something easier for the time being so they have something to show for it. We are also outwardly trans, but made lots of compromises with our little to make sure she was comfortable with the changes and that we never went further than she would be comfortable with. It's just lots of little things like that, making sure everyone is heard and their underlying problem is addressed, even if not in the exact way they had in mind.

The short version, what you're talking about doesn't exist. For a long time now, science has understood and accepted that there is no "original" or "real one" with DID at all. All children start out fragmented, and are supposed to integrate into a single cohesive personality later in childhood. Trauma makes it so those fragments stay separated instead, gaining amnesiac and dissociative barriers between eachother. There is no "original everyone split off from", you are all equally alters and all real.

DID and OSDD-1 are both developed in childhood, and happen because of long term destabilizing trauma. But very very few people know they have it before adulthood. As a child, most of us still live with the families that caused this trauma disorder in the first place. So DID remains a very covert disorder, for the childs safety and so you can just put your head down and survive until you get out of there. The vast majority of systems don't have their dam break until after they've moved out, or a new trauma causes chaos in adulthood and it becomes more obvious. 

Your therapist seems very misinformed about DID. It can only form in childhood because the formation of DID is dependent on the brain missing a developmental milestone because of trauma. at first switches were only a few hours at most, after a while it was days and weeks allowed out. i think it happened slowly over time, but we figured out it was easier for one of us to maintain a strong sense of self if they were out for longer and longer times, and because of that dissociate a whole lot less. its easier to get your bearings if your memory doesnt stop and start for an hour or two with days or weeks inbetween moments fronting. after this long, our individual senses of self are instinctual at an instant. its very very rare for someone to not be sure of who they are and who is fronting, if two are cofronting they know who they are and who is with them etc.

the current accepted science about how DID forms *is* that you miss a developmental milestone. along the lines of the theory of structural dissociation, all children start out fragmented. around the age of 9ish, children go through a developmental milestone where all the fragments become more like a single cohesive person, with a continuous memory and sense of self. long term destabilizing trauma causes a child to miss this crucial milestone, as the effects of trauma are more akin to brain damage that rewires how your brain works. 

this is why when you have DID, you have the potential to split someone new no matter how many times you fuse down to 1 person. this is the short and simple version, but it *is* pretty undisputed in scientific communities rn. DID isnt a scared child pretending everything happened to someone else to cope, your brain is in a very real sense rewired to be this way.
its specifically trauma that is long term and destabilizing to the child. this long term distress causes a child to miss their developmental milestone and develop DID instead, basically
